{"notes":"DRAFT, NOT POSTED. To: mls@ietf.org, cc the draft-ietf-mls-extensions editor. Needs Mark's OK before sending.

Subject: mls-extensions-11 §4.9: zero-length authenticated_data in a safe_aad group

Interop table note from the IETF 127 hackathon.

Setup: mimid (OpenMLS with mls-extensions-11) hosts a MIMI room whose GroupContext lists safe_aad. A stock mls-rs client joins by external Commit. mls-rs has no SafeAAD support, so unless the application sets it, authenticated_data is zero-length.

Result: mimid refuses the Commit. Its SafeAAD decode reaches end of input before the aad_items<V> length. With the application passing the single byte 0x00 (a SafeAAD with no items), the join works.

| Sender | authenticated_data | mimid (receiver) |
|---|---|---|
| mls-rs, default | zero-length | refused |
| mls-rs, app passes 0x00 | 00 | accepted |
| OpenMLS + extensions-11 | 00 | accepted |

The text we read this from:

§4.9: "If the safe_aad component in the app_data_dictionary extension is present in the GroupContext (see Section 5), the entire authenticated_data field is framed as a SafeAAD struct ..." and "If safe_aad is present, but none of the "safe" AAD components have data to send in a particular message, the aad_items is a zero-length vector."

§5: "If the safe_aad component is present, even with an empty list, ... in the GroupContext, then the authenticated_data field is a SafeAAD struct as defined in Section 4.9."

We read this as: the empty SafeAAD is 0x00, and zero-length authenticated_data is not a SafeAAD. The draft does not say what a receiver does with one. Two stacks can differ here, and one of them will refuse the other's messages.

Suggested text, either one, after the zero-length vector sentence in §4.9:

  Option 1: "A SafeAAD with no items is encoded as the single byte 0x00. A receiver MAY reject a message whose authenticated_data is not a SafeAAD struct."

  Option 2: "A receiver MAY treat a zero-length authenticated_data as a SafeAAD with no items."

Option 1 keeps one encoding per value. Option 2 lets clients without SafeAAD support send messages that carry no safe items. We implement Option 1's reading today and can switch.

Mark Atwood"}

d192f7f (branch core-safeaad): kept strict per mls-extensions-11 §4.9 (decision mimid-1wgh.71, for Mark to judge); tests pin refusal in Member and Observer; docs note; WG clarification drafted in notes, not posted.
